Model it as a complete architectural asset with a legible public face, believable side and service elevations, and construction logic appropriate to its use. The named object must be identifiable in neutral clay material before labels, color, and glow are applied.

Silhouette and proportion: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible. Keep the working envelope near 18 meters wide, 14 meters deep, and 9 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Adventurer Academy Exterior; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Model a coherent foundation, frame or load-bearing wall system, layered facade or structural depth, human-scale access, glazing or openings with frames, weather and drainage treatment, service access, and credible transitions between materials. Required visible components are primary massing, roof line, entrance, window system, facade material breaks, service side, foundation. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary weathered stone, aged timber, dark iron, leather or cloth where appropriate, earth, ember orange, arcane cyan. grounded dark-fantasy frontier; stone, timber, iron, leather, practical guild and settlement construction around a colossal descending dungeon gate. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: cute stacked blob monsters, plastic medieval props, uniform fantasy village kits. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Use soot, mineral deposits, damp staining, tool wear, patched timber, rubbed leather, hammer marks, repaired iron, and age only where construction and use justify them. Place it on the parcel, terrain shelf, dock edge, modular foundation, or interior footprint named by the blueprint. Public access faces navigation and social space; service access faces the alley, utility corridor, backstage zone, waterfront service edge, or maintenance route. Foundation, stairs, ramps, porches, piles, retaining walls, and terrain transitions must meet the environment without floating gaps. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Keep entrances, shutters, gates, windows, awnings, stairs, ramps, elevators, signs, lighting, roof equipment, and service components separable whenever gameplay or state changes may need them. Expected hooks include transform, material-state, damage, pickup, or placement hook only where gameplay requires it. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use modular floor, wall, roof, stair, rail, counter, doorway, foundation, and major structural collision. Walkable areas, entrances, windows used for gameplay, and service openings must match the visible model, while trim, roof equipment, cables, fasteners, and inaccessible facade detail remain simplified or nonblocking. Use positive Z as the principal entrance, public face, or module-forward direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at ground level or the documented connection plane near the footprint center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve massing, entrances, openings, supports, and skyline in every LOD. Repeating windows, panels, rails, trim, and structural members should use shared geometry or instancing. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 39,000 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 18,000 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 6,000 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Adventurer Academy Exterior is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

Model it as a production-ready environmental or interactive prop with a recognizable purpose, coherent assembly, correct scale, and town-specific materials. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use. Keep the working envelope near 1.2 meters wide, 0.9 meters deep, and 1.2 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Required visible components are heavy structural body, working face, firebox, striking surface, or cooling vessel, stable base or stand, handles, tuyere, lid, or tool grip where required, heat, impact, scale, and soot zones, service or cleanout access, floor clearance and nearby tool interaction. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary weathered stone, aged timber, dark iron, leather or cloth where appropriate, earth, ember orange, arcane cyan. grounded dark-fantasy frontier; stone, timber, iron, leather, practical guild and settlement construction around a colossal descending dungeon gate. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: cute stacked blob monsters, plastic medieval props, uniform fantasy village kits. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Use soot, mineral deposits, damp staining, tool wear, patched timber, rubbed leather, hammer marks, repaired iron, and age only where construction and use justify them. Place it on a named ground, wall, ceiling, counter, shelf, dock, room, vehicle, terrain, water, or gameplay socket appropriate to its use. Every foot, base, root, bracket, anchor, contact edge, and suspension point must sit flush or visibly explain how it is supported. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Separate parts that may open, rotate, light, display, receive an item, emit particles, take damage, change material, or connect to another system. Expected hooks include hinged, sliding, folding, or removable access state, pickup, open, consume, empty, stack, carry, or discard state. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve silhouette and interaction points, sharing repeated hardware and moving only microdetail into materials at lower LODs. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 18,720 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 8,640 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 2,880 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: The primary body and functional secondary parts must identify the object before labels or color. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Blacksmith Cooling Barrel is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Dungeon Lever is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

Expected hooks include day, night, powered, warning, and damaged light states. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: The primary body and functional secondary parts must identify the object before labels or color. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

Place it on a named ground, wall, ceiling, counter, shelf, dock, room, vehicle, terrain, water, or gameplay socket appropriate to its use. Every foot, base, root, bracket, anchor, contact edge, and suspension point must sit flush or visibly explain how it is supported. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Separate parts that may open, rotate, light, display, receive an item, emit particles, take damage, change material, or connect to another system. Expected hooks include day, night, powered, warning, and damaged light states. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve silhouette and interaction points, sharing repeated hardware and moving only microdetail into materials at lower LODs. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 18,720 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 8,640 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: The primary body and functional secondary parts must identify the object before labels or color. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Dungeon Torch is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

materialPlan.masonryRule: Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling.
materialPlan.woodRule: Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use.
materialPlan.flexibleRule: Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling.
materialPlan.emissiveRule: Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure.

It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Expected hooks include transform, material-state, damage, pickup, or placement hook only where gameplay requires it. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Home Potion Shelf is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB.
